claims.text: Applying a TiB2 coating to boride-based components will improve their resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion.
The TiB2 coating will form a stable, protective interfacial layer.
The TiB2 interfacial layer will resist chemical attack by molten aluminum.
The TiB2 layer will minimize diffusion of aluminum into the boride substrate.
Typical operating temperatures for hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment are approximately 660–750°C.
TiB2 has high chemical stability in molten aluminum.
TiB2 has low solubility in molten aluminum.
The chemical stability and low solubility of TiB2 prevent the formation of detrimental intermetallic compounds.
Suppressing intermetallic formation and aluminum diffusion enhances molten-aluminum corrosion resistance.
TiB2-coated components will have significantly lower corrosion rates than uncoated boride-based components under identical conditions.
The TiB2 coating will improve corrosion resistance by at least 50% relative to the uncoated baseline.
The improvement will persist provided that the operating temperature remains below the thermal-stability limit of TiB2.
The improvement will persist only while the coating remains intact and free of significant mechanical damage.
The magnitude of improvement depends on the quality and uniformity of the TiB2 coating.
The magnitude of improvement depends on the composition of the boride substrate and molten aluminum alloy.
